commentary_summary: Panamax utilisation fell 1.2 percentage points in week 31 as the tonne-miles index weakened and Baltic rates softened; vessel capacity at anchor/port declined MoM as more vessels moved underway. | North Atlantic continued to ease due to muted demand and a lack of fresh inquiries, while South Atlantic stayed broadly steady after showing early signs of support that failed to sustain. | In contrast, the Pacific saw increased ballast congestion due to increased demand from Australia and Indonesia, followed by a new US–Indonesia trade deal reducing tariffs to 19% from 32%.
